children: The big news in the first hour of trading is Brent hitting $100 a barrel for the first time since July as fighting escalates across the Middle East, sending European energy stocks to the brink of a new record high.

The STOXX oil and gas index is up 0.8% (.SXEP), roughly 0.5% shy of its early May peak. Defensive utilities stocks (.SX6P) are also performing strongly, but outside that most sectors are under pressure, and the broad STOXX 600 is down 0.6%.
Perhaps more worrying for Europe, given the state of gas storage in the north of the continent, is front month gas prices are up another 4%. (TFMBMc1)
Movers that aren't to do with the war and energy are retail stocks, with the sector off 1.5% at a three-month low, weighed down by weaker than expected second quarter profit at Inditex.
The Zara owner's shares are down 3%.
